_doc: CANONICAL-CHECK declarations for financial tables whose CREATE migration is ALREADY APPLIED to production and therefore immutable (scripts/verify-applied-migrations-immutable.mjs; editing one makes db-migrate refuse to migrate and red-lines every backend pre-deploy). The declaration requirement in scripts/verify-no-duplicate-financial-ledger.mjs is not waived by this file -- it is RELOCATED. Each entry carries the same content the in-migration block would: the money concept, and an explicit naming of every colliding canonical ledger with a stated reason the new table is distinct. A declaration here is honoured ONLY when the named migration exists on disk AND actually CREATEs that table, so this file cannot declare a table into existence or cover a table it does not name.
_when_to_use: ONLY for a table whose CREATE migration was already applied before the omission was caught. A NEW table still declares INSIDE its own migration -- that is the cheaper path and it stays the default. Adding an entry here is a deliberate act with the applied timestamp recorded next to it.
_added: 2026-09-30 by Claude Lead. main was RED on verify:no-duplicate-financial-ledger for both tables below, blocking every seat's PR. Verified red by running the guard against origin/main content, not inferred from one PR.

accounting.expenses_review_queue.why_not_in_migration: already applied to production when the omission was caught; applied migrations are immutable
accounting.expenses_review_queue.text: -- CANONICAL-CHECK: money concept = NONE. accounting.expenses_review_queue is not a ledger and holds no money of its own. GRAIN: one row per AUTH-089-voided accounting.expenses row that carries no vendor_document_number, i.e. a row whose claimed duplicate cannot be confirmed from the data alone and can be resolved only by a human reading the source document. It SNAPSHOTS identifying fields (load, date, amount, memo) from the expense plus the live row AUTH-089 claimed it duplicated, so a reviewer sees both sides without re-deriving the match. CANONICAL LEDGER FOR EXPENSES REMAINS accounting.expenses -- this table never inserts, updates or voids a row there, posts no GL, carries no debit/credit, and is read by no posting path. It is a review worklist pointing AT accounting.expenses by foreign key. Removing every row in it would change no balance and no financial statement. No registry concept collides with this name (the registry has no 'expense' concept); the declaration is required because 'accounting' is a financial schema.

driver_finance.settlement_line_item_spli.why_not_in_migration: already applied to production when the omission was caught; applied migrations are immutable
driver_finance.settlement_line_item_spli.text: -- CANONICAL-CHECK: money concept = settlement line ITEM DETAIL, not settlement value. COLLIDES WITH driver_finance.driver_settlements AND WITH driver_finance.settlement_lines, and is distinct from BOTH, deliberately. driver_finance.driver_settlements remains THE canonical settlement ledger: this table creates no settlement, holds no gross/deduction/net, and never changes what a driver is paid. driver_finance.settlement_lines remains THE canonical settlement line ledger and remains the ONLY source of settlement value: this table never inserts a line, never alters a line's amount, and its rows sum to the amount of the ONE line they explain -- they redistribute nothing. GRAIN: one row per constituent item of a single pre-existing settlement_lines row that a historical AlwaysTrack import materialized as one generic extra_pay row with item_id NULL, collapsing 2-5 real document lines into one. The 17 affected lines sit in settlements 5769-5819, which are closed and verified 51/51 against AlwaysTrack and are never re-opened (owner ruling), so the item detail is recorded BESIDE the signed document rather than by editing it. Append-only, WORM-protected by 202614710000_worm_settlement_line_item_splits.sql. The permanent engine-side fix ships in the same migration: a NOT VALID check constraint on driver_finance.settlement_lines requiring item_id on every FUTURE extra_pay line, so the next import cannot recreate the defect; NOT VALID grandfathers the 17 legacy rows instead of retroactively failing closed settlements.

driver_finance.feed_intakes.why_not_in_migration: already applied to production when the omission was caught; applied migrations are immutable
driver_finance.feed_intakes.text: -- CANONICAL-CHECK: money concept = NONE. driver_finance.feed_intakes is the FEED GATE intake register: one row per fed subject (settlement / load / expense / bill / invoice / factoring statement / fuel import / batch) with its open/passed/blocked/closed status, and the one-settlement-at-a-time rule per driver. It holds no amount, no debit/credit and no balance; it posts nothing and no posting path reads it as money. The canonical ledgers stay where they are: settlement value in driver_finance.driver_settlements / driver_finance.settlement_lines, the books in accounting.journal_entries. The migration's own header said 'CANONICAL-CHECK: driver_finance.*' mid-line, which the guard's line-start pattern does not read.

driver_finance.feed_intake_checks.why_not_in_migration: already applied to production when the omission was caught; applied migrations are immutable
driver_finance.feed_intake_checks.text: -- CANONICAL-CHECK: money concept = NONE. driver_finance.feed_intake_checks is the WORM check history of a feed intake: one row per check per run (pass / fail / na, what is missing, where to fix it). No amount, no balance, no posting; it is evidence that a fed document was verified before it moved on. It duplicates no ledger: driver_finance.driver_settlements, driver_finance.settlement_lines and accounting.journal_entries remain the only stores of the money the checks look at.

accounting.deposits.why_not_in_migration: already applied to production when the omission was caught; applied migrations are immutable
accounting.deposits.text: -- CANONICAL-CHECK: money concept = BANK DEPOSIT DOCUMENT (QuickBooks 'Make Deposit'). accounting.deposits is a source document: the deposit slip that moves receipts already in Undeposited Funds to a bank account (total_receipts_cents - cash_back_cents = amount_deposited_cents). Its GL effect is posted once through the posting engine as source type bank_deposit (DR the bank's ledger account / CR undeposited funds) and the entry is stamped on the row (journal_entry_id); accounting.journal_entries remains THE ledger. It is not a second bank ledger: banking.bank_transactions remains the bank feed, and the bank line MATCHES the deposit as one document rather than the deposit storing a bank balance. It holds no running balance. Void = reversal (voided_at), never DELETE (WORM).

accounting.deposit_lines.why_not_in_migration: already applied to production when the omission was caught; applied migrations are immutable
accounting.deposit_lines.text: -- CANONICAL-CHECK: money concept = BANK DEPOSIT LINE: one row per receipt on a deposit slip (a customer payment from accounting.payments, a factoring advance from accounting.factoring_advances, or the cash-back line), each pointing at its source document by FK. The amount on a line is the amount of that receipt carried onto the slip; it creates no receivable or payment of its own and posts nothing by itself (the header posts the deposit). accounting.payments and accounting.factoring_advances remain the canonical receipt documents and accounting.journal_entries the ledger. WORM: lines are never deleted.

banking.bank_account_tieouts.why_not_in_migration: already applied to production when the omission was caught; applied migrations are immutable
banking.bank_account_tieouts.text: -- CANONICAL-CHECK: money concept = BANK-to-GL TIE-OUT EVIDENCE, not a balance store. One row per bank account per day: the feed's closing balance, the GL balance of the account's ledger_account_id COMPUTED from accounting.journal_entry_postings at run time, the difference, and how much of it is explained by feed-only / GL-only lines. Nothing reads gl_balance_cents as a balance: it is recomputed on every run and kept only as the dated record of what tied (bank-tieout.routes.ts shows the history). banking.bank_transactions remains the bank feed, banking.bank_accounts.current_balance_cents the feed's current balance, and accounting.journal_entries the ledger. No DELETE grant.

accounting.factoring_purchases.why_not_in_migration: already applied to production when the omission was caught; applied migrations are immutable
accounting.factoring_purchases.text: -- CANONICAL-CHECK: money concept = FACTORING PURCHASE DOCUMENT (one Faro wire). accounting.factoring_purchases is the source document the owner closes: gross, escrow reserve, cash reserve, fee, wire fee, advance and net to IH35, held to Faro's formula by CHECK constraints. It posts through the existing secured-borrowing funding poster via exactly ONE accounting.factoring_advances row per purchase (factoring_advance_id, 1:1), so no GL math is duplicated and accounting.journal_entries stays the ledger; the bank match lives on the bank line (banking.bank_transactions.matched_factoring_advance_id), not here. It is distinct from the factoring.* schema (factoring.batch / reserve_movement / letter_of_release), which is the factor-relationship ledger: a purchase records what Faro bought, not a second factoring ledger. Void, never delete.

accounting.factoring_purchase_lines.why_not_in_migration: already applied to production when the omission was caught; applied migrations are immutable
accounting.factoring_purchase_lines.text: -- CANONICAL-CHECK: money concept = FACTORING PURCHASE LINE: one row per invoice sold on a purchase (gross, escrow reserve, cash reserve, fee), linking invoice <-> customer <-> load <-> purchase. A purchase posts only when its header equals the sum of its live lines. The line is not a receivable and not a second invoice ledger: accounting.invoices remains THE invoice/A-R document (ASC 860 secured borrowing: A/R stays until the debtor pays) and accounting.journal_entries the ledger. It is distinct from factoring.* (the factor-relationship ledger). Money columns are frozen once the purchase is posted.

accounting.lease_lessee_schedule_period.why_not_in_migration: the creating migration is HELD (db/migrations/.held-migrations.json, block ROUND-321-LEASE-TO-OWN): the Lead validates CC-1's exact bytes on a Neon branch before applying, so the declaration is relocated here instead of editing the held file under review
accounting.lease_lessee_schedule_period.text: -- CANONICAL-CHECK: money concept = ASC 842 LESSEE AMORTIZATION SCHEDULE (a subledger), not a second ledger. One row per lease asset line per period: payment, interest, principal, liability open/close, ROU amortization/close and straight-line cost, with the bill and the accretion journal entry each period posted through. The GL balance of the lease liability and ROU asset is accounting.journal_entries (roles lease_liability / rou_asset); those accounts pool every lease, so the per-lease carrying amount can only come from this schedule, and lease-buyout.service.ts reads it from POSTED, non-voided periods only. accounting.lease_contract remains the contract document. WORM (void-not-delete) + FORCE RLS.

accounting.factoring_repurchase_due_even.why_not_in_migration: already applied to production when the omission was caught; applied migrations are immutable
accounting.factoring_repurchase_due_even.text: -- CANONICAL-CHECK: money concept = NONE posted - an OBLIGATION EVENT queue. One row per purchased account still open on day 95 of its purchase (the Faro repurchase deadline), awaiting the owner's decision (extend / confirm repurchase / mark collected). It carries the line's gross for context but writes no journal entry, posting, bill or payment; the repurchase itself posts later through Banking when the deduction or payment is matched. accounting.factoring_purchases / accounting.factoring_purchase_lines remain the purchase documents, accounting.invoices the receivable, accounting.journal_entries the ledger, and factoring.* the factor-relationship ledger. Append-only.

accounting.factoring_interest_accrual_ru.why_not_in_migration: already applied to production when the omission was caught; applied migrations are immutable
accounting.factoring_interest_accrual_ru.text: -- CANONICAL-CHECK: money concept = MONTH-END ACCRUAL RUN (a maker-checker approval document for one journal entry). One row per company and period: proposed by one user, approved by a second (maker <> checker), and only then does ONE journal entry post (DR 6830 Default Interest / CR 2155 Accrued Factoring Interest), stamped on the row (posted = has journal_entry_id). A rejected run posts nothing. It stores no balance: the accrued interest balance is account 2155 in accounting.journal_entries, the ledger. Distinct from factoring.* (factor-relationship ledger). A decided run never changes; never deleted.

accounting.factoring_interest_accrual_ru.why_not_in_migration: already applied to production when the omission was caught; applied migrations are immutable
accounting.factoring_interest_accrual_ru.text: -- CANONICAL-CHECK: money concept = ACCRUAL RUN COMPUTATION LINE: one row per open purchased account in a run, showing how the run's total was computed (net amount, cumulative contract interest, what earlier posted runs already accrued, this run's accrual; accrual = cumulative - previously accrued, CHECK-enforced). These are the run's working papers; they post nothing themselves (the run's one journal entry does) and are frozen once the run leaves 'proposed'. accounting.journal_entries remains the ledger and accounting.factoring_purchase_lines the purchased accounts.

accounting.faro_reserve_entries.why_not_in_migration: already applied to production when the omission was caught; applied migrations are immutable
accounting.faro_reserve_entries.text: -- CANONICAL-CHECK: money concept = FARO RESERVE REPORT LINE (the factor's statement line as a source document). One row per line of Faro's Escrow Reserve Entries (register escrow, GL 1230) or Cash Reserve Entries (register cash, GL 1235) report, as printed, plus its parsed kind; each reserve posting stamps it as source type faro_reserve_entry. It is the bank feed for the reserve register, not a ledger: the reserve balance is the GL of 1230 / 1235 in accounting.journal_entries, and the stored running and short-pay balances this table was created with were removed (KILL THE SECOND SYSTEM tables 10 + 11: 202615420600 dropped running_balance_cents and short_pay_balance_cents). Distinct from factoring.reserve_movement (factor-relationship ledger) and from driver_finance.escrow_ledger (driver escrow, a different money). Idempotent import; never deleted.

accounting.faro_cash_reserve_reclasses.why_not_in_migration: already applied to production when the omission was caught; applied migrations are immutable
accounting.faro_cash_reserve_reclasses.text: -- CANONICAL-CHECK: money concept = PERIOD-END PRESENTATION RECLASS document. One live row per company and period end: the cash reserve deficit at period end and the two journal entries it posted (DR 1235 / CR 2156 dated the period end, reversed the next day), so the balance sheet presents a negative reserve as a payable to Faro. It stores no balance: 1235 and 2156 balances are accounting.journal_entries, the ledger, and the deficit is read from that ledger when the reclass is made. Written once; history is never edited (a reclass whose entries were voided through the void engine may be posted again). Distinct from factoring.* and from driver_finance.escrow_ledger.

accounting.document_work_order_copies.why_not_in_migration: already applied to production when the omission was caught; applied migrations are immutable
accounting.document_work_order_copies.text: -- CANONICAL-CHECK: money concept = NONE. accounting.document_work_order_copies keeps the work order AS IT WAS when a bill or expense was linked to it (header, the print fields of unit / driver / vendor / company, line totals and lines), so the document opens and prints the work order it was entered against. Its totals are a frozen copy for printing, never read as money: accounting.bills / accounting.expenses remain the documents, maintenance.work_orders the live work order, and accounting.journal_entries the ledger. One writer (triggers on bills / bill_lines / expenses / expense_lines); WORM, never deleted.

Declarations relocated here, one per table, each read against its migration and its readers; none is a second ledger (stored balances in faro_reserve_entries were already dropped by 202615420600).
